description: Turns one pitch into a four-note seventh chord, with a choice of quality, inversion and voicing, and four separate pitch outputs

params.text: Transposes the whole chord, four and a half octaves either way from C4
Switches the chord quality over to one chosen from the major scale by the incoming pitch, and stops the quality knob and its jack from being read
Chooses how the four notes are spread: close, drop 2, drop 3 or spread; the lamp beside the name in use is lit
Chooses which note of the chord is at the bottom: root, first, second or third inversion; the lamp beside the name in use is lit
Chooses the chord: maj 7, min 7, dom 7 or halfdim; the lamp beside the name in use is lit, and none of it is read while harmon is on

inputs.text: The root pitch, added to the frequency knob at one volt per octave
Added to the voicing knob, one step of four per two and a half volts
Added to the inversion knob, one step of four per two and a half volts
Added to the quality knob, one step of four per two and a half volts; it is not read while harmon is on

outputs.text: The root of the chord, one volt per octave
The third of the chord, one volt per octave
The fifth of the chord, one volt per octave
The seventh of the chord, one volt per octave

notes: with nothing patched the four outputs give a C major seventh in close position, so the module is playing before anything reaches it.
bypassed, the root pitch input is copied to all four outputs.
